entities.name: Aḥmad Ibn-Muḥammad al- Maidānī
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Aḥmad Ibn-Muḥammad al-Maidānī, a prominent Persian lexicographer and literary scholar who died in 1124 CE, was a pivotal figure in the preservation and systematization of classical Arabic proverbs. Operating from Nishapur, a vibrant intellectual hub during the Seljuk period, al-Maidānī’s extensive scholarship contributed significantly to the philological traditions of the Islamic Golden Age. His work provided an invaluable resource for understanding the linguistic nuances, cultural values, and historical context embedded within the vast corpus of Arabic popular wisdom.

His magnum opus, *Majmaʿ al-Amthāl* (Collection of Proverbs), stands as an monumental achievement, compiling over 6,000 Arabic proverbs organized alphabetically. Beyond mere recitation, al-Maidānī meticulously provided the historical context, origin stories, and grammatical explanations for each entry, often referencing classical Arabic poetry and historical anecdotes. This comprehensive approach distinguished his collection, transforming it from a simple compilation into a foundational reference work for Arabists and literary scholars throughout the centuries. He also authored other works, though *Majmaʿ al-Amthāl* remains his most celebrated and enduring contribution.

The profound impact of al-Maidānī's *Majmaʿ al-Amthāl* resonated across the Islamic world, establishing itself as the authoritative and most widely cited collection of Arabic proverbs. It served as an essential pedagogical tool for students of Arabic language and literature and influenced subsequent generations of lexicographers, grammarians, and historians. His meticulous methodology set a new standard for philological inquiry, ensuring that the ephemeral wisdom of oral tradition was codified and preserved for posterity, thereby enriching the intellectual heritage of the Classical and post-Classical eras.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Aḥmad Ibn-Muḥammad al- Maidānī's *Majmaʿ al-Amthāl* became the definitive collection of Arabic proverbs, preserving thousands of entries and influencing Arabic lexicography and literary studies for nearly a millennium. His work solidified a key aspect of Arabic cultural heritage.
